bodies.name: Sun
bodies.short_description: The warm, luminous anchor of this small prototype system.
bodies.full_description: The Sun is the star at the center of our solar system. Its gravity holds the planets, dwarf planets, asteroids, and comets in orbit, while its energy powers the climate and chemistry of Earth.
bodies.atmosphere: Hydrogen and helium plasma; no solid surface
bodies.composition: About 74% hydrogen and 24% helium by mass, with heavier elements making up the remainder.
interesting_facts: Contains more than 99% of the solar system's total mass.
Light from the Sun reaches Earth in about 8 minutes 20 seconds.
Its visible surface is called the photosphere.

bodies.name: Earth
bodies.short_description: A blue world with a hint of green, orbiting in the inner system.
bodies.full_description: Earth is a rocky planet with stable surface oceans and a nitrogen-rich atmosphere. It is the only world currently known to support life, with a dynamic climate shaped by its atmosphere, oceans, and magnetic field.
bodies.atmosphere: About 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, and 1% argon and trace gases
bodies.composition: A rocky silicate mantle and crust surrounding an iron-rich core.
interesting_facts: Liquid surface water covers roughly 71% of the planet.
Earth's magnetic field helps deflect charged particles from the solar wind.
Its atmosphere and oceans continuously exchange heat and moisture.

bodies.name: Mars
bodies.short_description: A rust-colored outer neighbor on a wider representative orbit.
bodies.full_description: Mars is a cold, dusty terrestrial planet with a thin atmosphere and a surface marked by impact craters, volcanoes, valleys, and polar ice. Its iron-rich minerals give the landscape its characteristic red color.
bodies.atmosphere: About 95% carbon dioxide, 2.7% nitrogen, and 1.6% argon
bodies.composition: Rocky silicates with an iron-rich core and iron oxide dust on the surface.
interesting_facts: Olympus Mons is the largest known volcano in the solar system.
A Martian day, called a sol, is only about 40 minutes longer than an Earth day.
Mars has two small moons named Phobos and Deimos.

bodies.name: Mercury
bodies.short_description: A small, cratered world racing through the innermost orbit.
bodies.full_description: Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest to the Sun. Without a substantial atmosphere to hold heat, it swings between extremes of day and night, and its heavily cratered surface preserves a long record of impacts.
bodies.average_temperature: About 167°C global average; −173°C to 427°C between night and day
bodies.rotation_period: 58.6 Earth days (sidereal); 176 Earth days solar day
bodies.atmosphere: Effectively none; a tenuous exosphere of oxygen, sodium, hydrogen, helium, and potassium
bodies.composition: An iron-rich core filling most of the planet's radius, enclosed by a thin silicate mantle and crust.
interesting_facts: A single Mercury year lasts only 88 Earth days.
Its day-night temperature swing is the largest of any planet, from about −173°C to 427°C.
Mercury rotates three times for every two orbits it completes around the Sun.

bodies.name: Venus
bodies.short_description: A veiled, scorching twin of Earth beneath permanent cloud cover.
bodies.full_description: Venus is close to Earth in size and mass but has a dense carbon dioxide atmosphere that traps heat in a runaway greenhouse effect. Its surface is hot enough to melt lead, and clouds of sulfuric acid hide the landscape from view.
bodies.rotation_period: 243 Earth days, retrograde (sidereal); 117 Earth days solar day
bodies.atmosphere: About 96.5% carbon dioxide and 3.5% nitrogen, with layers of sulfuric acid cloud
bodies.composition: A rocky silicate planet with an iron core, largely resurfaced by widespread volcanism.
interesting_facts: Venus spins backwards compared with most planets, so the Sun would rise in the west.
A sidereal day lasts longer than its year: 243 Earth days to spin once against 224.7 to orbit the Sun.
Surface pressure is roughly 92 times that of Earth at sea level.

bodies.name: Jupiter
bodies.short_description: The system's largest planet, banded in cloud and circled by storms.
bodies.full_description: Jupiter is a gas giant more massive than all the other planets combined. Its rapid rotation stretches the clouds into alternating belts and zones, and its Great Red Spot is a storm that has persisted for centuries.
bodies.atmosphere: About 90% hydrogen and 10% helium by volume, with traces of methane, ammonia, and water
bodies.composition: Mostly hydrogen and helium, with a deep layer of metallic hydrogen and a diffuse dense core.
interesting_facts: Jupiter is more than eleven times wider than Earth.
The Great Red Spot is a storm wider than Earth.
Its four largest moons, Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto, were first observed by Galileo in 1610.

bodies.name: Saturn
bodies.short_description: A pale gas giant framed by the system's broadest ring system.
bodies.full_description: Saturn is a gas giant best known for its bright rings, which are made almost entirely of water ice. Its low density and rapid rotation flatten it visibly at the poles.
bodies.atmosphere: About 96% hydrogen and 3% helium by volume, with traces of methane and ammonia
bodies.composition: Mostly hydrogen and helium surrounding a metallic hydrogen interior, with a mean density lower than water.
interesting_facts: Saturn's mean density is lower than that of water, so it would float in a large enough ocean.
Its main rings span about 282,000 km but are typically only tens of metres thick.
Titan, its largest moon, has a thick nitrogen atmosphere and lakes of liquid hydrocarbons.

bodies.name: Uranus
bodies.short_description: A tilted ice giant rolling on its side through the outer system.
bodies.full_description: Uranus is an ice giant whose axis is tipped close to its orbital plane, so the planet appears to roll on its side as it orbits. Methane in its upper atmosphere absorbs red light, giving the planet a pale blue-green color.
bodies.atmosphere: About 83% hydrogen, 15% helium, and 2% methane by volume
bodies.composition: A hydrogen and helium envelope over an icy mantle of water, ammonia, and methane, around a small rocky core.
interesting_facts: Uranus is tilted about 98°, most likely by a collision early in its history.
Each pole receives about 42 Earth years of continuous sunlight, then 42 years of darkness.
It was the first planet found with a telescope, in 1781.

bodies.name: Neptune
bodies.short_description: The most distant planet, a deep blue ice giant of fierce winds.
bodies.full_description: Neptune is the outermost planet and the smallest of the four giants. Despite receiving little sunlight, it drives the fastest winds measured in the solar system and shows dark storms that appear and fade over years.
bodies.atmosphere: About 80% hydrogen, 19% helium, and 1.5% methane by volume
bodies.composition: A hydrogen and helium envelope over a mantle of water, ammonia, and methane above a rocky core.
interesting_facts: Neptune's winds reach roughly 2,000 km/h, the fastest measured in the solar system.
It was found in 1846 by following mathematical predictions, before anyone observed it.
One Neptune year lasts about 165 Earth years; it completed its first full orbit since discovery in 2011.

missions.description: Begin your exploration with a journey to our blue home world.
missions.objective: Travel to Earth and arrive at its observation point.

missions.title: Red Planet Approach
missions.description: Set a course for the rust-colored neighbor of Earth.
missions.objective: Travel to Mars and arrive at its observation point.

missions.description: Observe the star that anchors this solar system from a representative viewpoint.
missions.objective: Travel to the Sun's observation point.

missions.description: Explore two rocky worlds in a short guided itinerary.
missions.objective: Arrive at Earth, then travel to Mars.

missions.title: Stellar Neighborhood
missions.description: Discover the scientific profiles of our star and its two featured planets.
missions.objective: Open scientific details for the Sun, then Earth, then Mars after starting this mission.
